profile.name: Moin Shadab
profile.tagline: Building high-concurrency backend software, open-source enterprise ERPs, and ground-up protocol engines.
profile.availability: Available for high-impact backend & systems engineering roles
profile.bio: I don't build superficial wrappers. I build raw backend platforms: an open-source enterprise ERP (MSERP) handling multi-warehouse stock, GST billing, and payroll, plus an international email engine built from scratch with raw IMAP stream sockets and a hybrid MySQL + CouchDB architecture. My code runs where failure isn't an option — backed by 2 years of industrial PLC safety automation discipline.

experiences.description: Programmed Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) for manufacturing automation lines. Designed deterministic control logic under tight hardware execution limits.
experiences.highlight: Engineered zero-tolerance safety interlocking logic and sensor data polling systems for factory automation lines.

story.headline: The Blueprint
story.alternativeHeadline: From Industrial Automation to Ground-Up Backend Protocol Engines
story.lede: I started where an unhandled condition didn't throw an HTTP 500 error — it caused a pneumatic cylinder in a physical factory line to jam. That discipline in zero-tolerance reliability, deterministic states, and hardware timing shaped my entire approach when stepping into cloud software: building open-source enterprise ERPs, dual-database storage pipelines, and raw IMAP stream socket engines.

chapters.title: The Deterministic Floor
chapters.subtitle: Learning safety interlocking & millisecond scan loops
chapters.content: Before writing high-throughput REST APIs, my engineering sandbox was industrial control. In factory automation, you don't have the luxury of retrying an asynchronous promise if you miss a physical safety barrier. Every line of ladder logic runs in deterministic scan cycles of 5 to 20 milliseconds.
chapters.quote: If a backend controller fails in production, an API returns 500. If an industrial PLC interlock fails, machinery stops or breaks. That standard never left me.
chapters.highlight: Programmed Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) with zero-tolerance safety interlocking logic, sensor polling protocols, and discrete hardware registers.

chapters.title: From Relays to Distributed Sockets
chapters.subtitle: Bridging low-level execution with modern software architecture
chapters.content: Transitioning from physical PLC logic to large-scale backend systems felt natural: memory allocation, lock contention, race conditions, and idempotent transactions are the software twins of electrical relays and interlocking switches. I dove deep into C++, Java, and PHP systems programming, obsessed with understanding what happens under the surface of frameworks.
chapters.quote: Frameworks come and go, but protocols, buffer allocation, and atomic transactions remain constant.
chapters.highlight: Mastered concurrency, database indexing internals, TCP/IP packet flows, and foundational Data Structures & Algorithms.

chapters.title: Advanced Microdevices & The Enterprise Reality
chapters.subtitle: Designing software where inventory mistakes cost millions
chapters.content: Joining Advanced Microdevices Pvt. Ltd. as a backend developer, I took ownership of core enterprise software suites. In an industrial enterprise, inventory isn't a simple counter in a database: items move across multiple physical warehouses, get locked in transit, require GST-compliant invoicing, and integrate with barcode scanners on the factory floor.
chapters.quote: A single race condition in warehouse checkout can corrupt physical stock counts across continents. Pessimistic database locks are non-negotiable.
chapters.highlight: Engineered multi-warehouse inventory systems using row-level pessimistic locking, automated GST ledger calculation engines, and barcode verification pipelines.

chapters.title: The Dual-DB International Email Engine
chapters.subtitle: Refusing SaaS wrappers: RFC-3501 IMAP sockets + Hybrid Storage
chapters.content: Most web teams that need email capabilities pay for Mailgun, Sendgrid, or third-party wrappers. When tasked with building an internal international email client, I chose to construct it from first principles. I opened raw SSL stream sockets directly to remote IMAP/SMTP servers (`stream_socket_client`), hand-crafted the RFC-3501 state machine, wrote MIME multi-part chunk decoders, and designed a hybrid Dual-Database architecture.
chapters.quote: MySQL manages indexed folder metadata and foreign keys; CouchDB stores unstructured JSON mail payloads and raw document attachments. Fast indexing with infinite document scalability.
chapters.highlight: Built an International Email Client bypassing SaaS dependencies: raw socket streams + MySQL relational indexing + CouchDB NoSQL message documents + Redis background queue workers.

chapters.title: MSERP: Open Source Enterprise ERP
chapters.subtitle: Giving back a production-grade suite with working modules
chapters.content: Commercial ERPs like SAP and Oracle charge exorbitant licensing fees, locking small manufacturing and healthcare businesses out. I architected and open-sourced MSERP — a fully functional, complete enterprise ERP platform featuring multi-warehouse inventory, double-entry GST billing, hospital management (EMR), sales pipelines, and payroll.
chapters.quote: Enterprise software should not be an inaccessible fortress. MSERP proves that clean architecture, deterministic transactions, and modern backends can be completely open.
chapters.highlight: Shipped MSERP on GitHub with complete working modules, test coverage, and documentation for community deployment.

chapters.title: Payment Sockets & Financial Integrity
chapters.subtitle: Securing high-volume transactions with cryptographic checksums
chapters.content: Integrated Indian PhonePe payment gateway API with strict SHA-256 webhook signature verification, replay attack prevention, and idempotent reconciliation routines. Published public integration reference guides to help fellow engineers handle webhook state machines without leaking transactions.
chapters.quote: When money is moving across wire APIs, assume every network packet can be delayed, duplicated, or spoofed. Verify every checksum at the gate.
chapters.highlight: Architected zero-drop payment processing pipelines with automatic reconciliation and published the open reference guide.

chapters.title: Architecting for Concurrency & Scale
chapters.subtitle: Available for high-impact backend & systems engineering
chapters.content: Today, I continue to push the boundaries of backend engineering — building high-concurrency systems, exploring distributed messaging, and contributing to open-source infrastructure. I bring the rare combination of low-level hardware discipline and high-level enterprise software craftsmanship to every team I join.
chapters.quote: Software is only as good as its failure modes. I build systems designed to stay standing.
chapters.highlight: Actively seeking ambitious backend, infrastructure, and systems engineering roles globally.

faqs.q: Why use a Dual-Database architecture (MySQL + CouchDB) for the email engine?
faqs.a: Relational databases (MySQL) excel at structured queries, foreign keys, unread counts, and folder trees. However, storing varied MIME multipart structures, arbitrary email attachments, and nested JSON payloads in relational tables causes table bloat and schema migration headaches. CouchDB provides document-level JSON storage and revision tracking, while MySQL handles lightning-fast relational queries.

faqs.q: How does your 2-year background in PLC automation benefit software engineering?
faqs.a: PLC programming teaches zero-tolerance discipline: you cannot afford unhandled edge cases when physical machines are moving. It instills an instinct for deterministic states, race conditions, hardware timeouts, and sensor polling loops — all of which directly translate into building resilient, crash-proof backend systems.

faqs.q: What makes MSERP different from other open-source ERP projects?
faqs.a: Many open-source ERP templates are shallow starter kits with mock data. MSERP is engineered with production-ready business logic: pessimistic database locks (`lockForUpdate`) for inventory deduction, automatic GST tax tier calculations, and full hospital EMR workflows.

faqs.q: Are you open to remote or international backend roles?
faqs.a: Yes! I am available for full-time backend engineering, systems architecture, and infrastructure roles with high-impact teams across the globe.

codeSnippets.title: imap_socket_parser.php
codeSnippets.code:
<?php
namespace App\Services\Mail;

class ImapSocketClient {
    private $stream;
    private int $tagCount = 0;

    public function connect(string $host, int $port = 993): bool {
        $context = stream_context_create(['ssl' => ['verify_peer' => false]]);
        $this->stream = @stream_socket_client(
            "ssl://{$host}:{$port}", $errno, $errstr, 15, STREAM_CLIENT_CONNECT, $context
        );
        if (!$this->stream) throw new \RuntimeException("IMAP socket failed: {$errstr}");
        return true;
    }

    public function fetchMessageToCouchDB(string $msgId, \App\Services\CouchDbClient $couch) {
        $rawPayload = $this->command("FETCH {$msgId} (BODY[])");
        $parsed = \App\Services\MimeParser::decode($rawPayload);
        return $couch->insertDocument([
            'msg_id' => $msgId,
            'headers' => $parsed['headers'],
            'html_body' => $parsed['html'],
            'plain_body' => $parsed['text'],
            'attachments' => $parsed['attachments']
        ]);
    }
}

codeSnippets.title: MsErpCoreController.php
codeSnippets.code:
<?php
namespace App\Http\Controllers\Api;

use App\Models\Inventory;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

class MsErpCoreController extends Controller {
    public function deductStock(Request $req) {
        $validated = $req->validate([
            'sku' => 'required|string',
            'qty' => 'required|integer|min:1'
        ]);

        return DB::transaction(function() use ($validated) {
            $item = Inventory::where('sku', $validated['sku'])->lockForUpdate()->firstOrFail();
            if ($item->stock_qty < $validated['qty']) {
                return response()->json(['error' => 'Insufficient Stock'], 422);
            }
            $item->decrement('stock_qty', $validated['qty']);
            return response()->json(['status' => 'MSERP_SUCCESS', 'remaining' => $item->stock_qty]);
        });
    }
}
